name: Yuchen Zhao
bio: Yuchen Zhao is a researcher in digital media, XR, human-computer interaction, and human-centered AI. Her doctoral research, including the BioVR project, explored how physiological data can be incorporated into XR to create adaptive interaction mechanisms that respond to users’ physical and emotional states. Her broader interests include digital heritage, new media storytelling, and interactive experience design. She is currently a Postdoctoral Associate at the Yale School of Nursing, where her work focuses on AI-enabled digital health interventions.

name: Daniel Phelps
bio: Daniel Phelps is a media artist, designer, and educator whose work connects large-scale making, spatial storytelling, and advanced technology into a single practice. His research and creative work have been sponsored by NASA, the Oak Ridge National Labs, the Create-X program, the Wagner Foundation, and the PSC/CUNY Research Foundation. He holds a Ph.D. in Digital Media from Georgia Tech and has led academic programs spanning robotics, XR, and media production across more than 20 years of teaching. He currently serves as faculty for the School of Literature, Media, and Communication at the Georgia Institute of Technology.

name: Patrick Fiorilli
bio: Patrick Fiorilli is a writer, critic, and scholar of video games, literature, and media. His work is featured in scholarly journals like Game Studies and Angelaki, as well as in popular venues like the Los Angeles Review of Books and Bright Wall/Dark Room. He holds a Ph.D. in Digital Media from the Georgia Institute of Technology and has taught in the Media Arts and Design Program at the University of Chicago and in the Department of Radio/Television/Film at Northwestern University. He cohosts and produces the literature podcast Pynchon Pals, and writes a newsletter called Critical Theorycraft.

name: Joshua A. Fisher
bio: As an Associate Professor at Ball State University, Fisher’s work explores how emerging technologies shape the ways people create, interpret, and participate in the world around them. As a digital humanist and designer, he builds and studies interactive systems with a particular interest in human agency, community storytelling, learning, and how people negotiate meaning with increasingly intelligent and spatial technologies.

name: Rebecca Rouse
bio: Phd is an Associate Professor in Media Arts, Aesthetics, and Narration and co-director of PlayLab in the Division of Game Development at University of Skövde, Sweden. Rouse’s research spans artistic creation, design with XR technologies, media history, and critical pedagogy. Her focus is the development of new forms of storytelling with new technologies in media theater, games, and interactive narrative. Rouse is the Executive Editor of the ICIDS Book series Interactive Storytelling Art (Play Story Press), a member of the Editorial Board for the journals Digital Creativity, JIB: Journal of Interactive Books, and JINR: Journal of Interactive Narrative Research. Rouse is a co-founder of PlayLab, an interdisciplinary research and performance platform for innovating at the nexus of games, games technology, and the performing arts.

name: Geoffrey Thomas
bio: I create interactive, multimedia experiences that entertain, inform, and engage. I've done this as a designer, artist, curator, teacher, and manager. My work moves across mediums, combining painting, drawing, photography, music, animation, filmmaking, electronics, digital media, and code.
